question: Walk me through issuing a new custom token on Stellar from scratch.

golden.answer: There is no create-asset operation. An asset is an asset code plus issuer. Fund a separate issuing account and distribution account, set any authorization flags first, have the distribution account open a trustline with `ChangeTrust`, then have the issuer pay the supply to it. Publish a stellar.toml (SEP-1). Locking the issuer afterwards stops further issuance; paying the asset back to the issuer burns it, because the issuer cannot hold its own asset.
keyFacts: A classic asset is defined by its asset code and issuing account.
The distribution account opens a trustline with ChangeTrust before it receives the asset.
The issuer creates supply by paying it to the distribution account.
Using distinct issuing and distribution accounts is recommended, not required.
avoid: Do NOT describe issuing a classic asset as deploying an ERC-20-style contract.
Do NOT claim that a dedicated createAsset operation exists in the protocol.
golden.notes: A SAC admin moved with set_admin can still mint after the issuer is locked; do not penalize an answer that adds this.

corroboration.claim: AUTH_REQUIRED and clawback are stamped on trustlines at creation, while AUTH_REVOCABLE lets the issuer revoke existing trustlines.

evidence.note: Exact quote: "When AUTH_REVOCABLE_FLAG is enabled, an issuer can revoke an existing trustline’s authorization ... With the AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG flag set, any *subsequent* trustlines established with this account will have clawbacks enabled."
Exact quote: "if (!isAuthRequired(issuer)) { tl.flags = AUTHORIZED_FLAG; } if (isClawbackEnabledOnAccount(issuer)) { tl.flags |= TRUSTLINE_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG; }"

evidence.note: It is best practice on the Stellar network to create two accounts when issuing an asset: 1) the issuing account and 2) the distribution account.
